title: How Much Electricity Does a Dehumidifier Use? Watts & Cost
h1: How Much Electricity Does a Dehumidifier Use?
dek: Forget the amps on the label — here's what a dehumidifier really draws, what it costs per day and per month, and how to compare models fairly.
description: How much electricity does a dehumidifier use? Typical watts by size, cost per day and per month at 2026 rates, and ENERGY STAR kWh ratings for popular models.
intro: So, how much electricity does a dehumidifier use? Most portable models draw roughly **230 to 560 watts** while the compressor is running — about 230–260 W for a 20- to 22-pint room unit and 400–560 W for a 50-pint basement model. Whole-house ducted systems can pull 800–1,400 W.

In dollars, ENERGY STAR rates a typical 50-pint unit at about 515–521 kWh a year, which works out to roughly $95 at the U.S. average residential rate of 18.44 cents per kWh (EIA, August 2026). Run a 500-watt unit for eight hours and you'll spend about 74 cents that day.

The pint number on the box and the amps on the nameplate don't tell you any of that. Below, we explain which numbers do, show real ratings for popular models, and walk through how to estimate your own bill.
topPicksLead: If running cost is your top priority, AEOCKY's 50-class chassis is the most efficient unit we track, though Midea's Cube 50 removes more water per day.

blocks.text: Two takeaways. The mainstream 50-pint models are effectively tied — all rated 2.01 L/kWh and within $2 a year of each other. And even the most efficient 50-class unit saves only about $15 a year at rated hours. Sizing and settings matter more than brand. Our [energy-efficient dehumidifier](/best/best-energy-efficient-dehumidifier/) ranking lists the current leaders.

sections.heading: Why the amps on the label overstate the draw

blocks.text: The nameplate on a 50-pint dehumidifier often lists 8 to 9 amps. That's a maximum used for wiring and circuit sizing, measured under harsher conditions than a typical basement. Multiply it by 115 volts and you get a figure near 1,000 watts, which looks like running draw but isn't. Frigidaire's older FHDD5034W1, for instance, was widely quoted at 978 watts from its nameplate, while its current successor carries the same ENERGY STAR rating as Midea's Cube 50.

sections.heading: Why your real bill is usually lower

blocks.text: The math above assumes the compressor runs the whole time, but a humidistat switches it off once the room reaches its target and back on as moisture returns. The first few days in a damp basement cost the most; after that, the unit is mostly topping off.

items: **Set a sensible target.** 45–50% is plenty for most rooms; see our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/).
**Size correctly.** An undersized unit runs nonstop; our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) helps you match capacity to space.
**Seal the space.** Close windows and vents so you're not drying the outdoors.
**Keep it clean.** A clogged filter or iced coil wastes power; see our [maintenance guide](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/).

blocks.text: A portable dehumidifier typically uses 230–560 watts while running, which for a 50-pint model works out to about $95 a year at ENERGY STAR's rated hours. Compare models on IEF and annual kWh, not pints or amps, and remember that right-sizing and a properly cycling humidistat save more than any brand switch. Wondering how it stacks up against cooling? Our [dehumidifier vs. air conditioner](/guides/dehumidifier-vs-air-conditioner/) guide covers the trade-offs.

faqs.q: How many watts does a dehumidifier use?
faqs.a: About 230–260 watts for a 20- to 22-pint room unit and roughly 400–560 watts for a 50-pint model while the compressor runs. Whole-house ducted units can draw 800–1,400 watts.

faqs.q: How much electricity does a dehumidifier use per day?
faqs.a: A 500-watt unit running eight hours uses about 4 kWh, roughly $0.74 at the national average rate. A 250-watt small-room unit over the same hours uses about 2 kWh, or $0.37.

faqs.q: How much electricity does a dehumidifier use per month?
faqs.a: At eight hours a day, a compact unit typically costs $10–$16 a month and a 50-pint unit $18–$25, at 18.44¢ per kWh. Your local rate and how often the humidistat cycles will move that number.

faqs.q: Does a dehumidifier run all the time?
faqs.a: No. A humidistat shuts the compressor off once the room reaches its set humidity and restarts it as moisture returns, so real use is usually well below a 24-hour estimate.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to run a dehumidifier or an air conditioner?
faqs.a: A dehumidifier is usually much cheaper; central AC compressors often draw 3,000–5,000 watts. They do different jobs, though: AC cools, while a dehumidifier removes moisture without much cooling.
